idea-plugin.name: Claude Terminal Tabs
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Terminal Tab Persistence for Rider / IntelliJ

Persists your Claude Code terminal sessions across IDE restarts — saved tabs come back with their names and auto-resume their conversations, so you can juggle multiple Claude sessions without losing them when you close Rider.

Features

  • Live status glyph on every tab — ● working, ⚠ waiting for input or a permission prompt, ✓ finished, ○ idle, ✕ exited. Driven by Claude Code hooks, so it lands within a fraction of a second. Hover the tab for the wording.
  • Remote Control on by default — a claude remote-control tab per project, so this machine's sessions are reachable from claude.ai/code and the Claude mobile app. Disable via remoteControl.enabled in ~/.claude/intellij-claude-terminal/config.json.
  • Tabs named from Claude's own summary of the conversation, read out of its session file — no turn spent on naming. /tab <name> overrides it and is never overwritten.
  • Race-condition-free identification of each tab via TERM_SESSION_ID mapping
  • Session save/restore across IDE restarts — your named tabs come back
  • Respects manual renames — if you rename a tab yourself, the plugin backs off

Requirements: Rider / IntelliJ 2026.1+ with the bundled Terminal plugin, and Claude Code CLI installed. Session detection is cross-platform (ProcessHandle); the bundled shell scripts branch on tasklist for Windows and ps elsewhere. Windows and macOS are exercised; Linux should work but is less tested.

Compatibility: Rider / IntelliJ 2026.1 and newer. On Rider 2026.1 the plugin coexists with the JetBrains AI Assistant chat tool window (the "AI Agents" panel: Junie / Claude Agent / Codex) and Anthropic's official Claude Code [Beta] plugin. This plugin manages terminal-launched Claude CLI sessions only — chat tabs in the AI Agents panel are managed by JetBrains and are not auto-restored here. Set Registry key claude.terminal.tabs.respectAiAgents to false to disable the coexistence notice in the log.

A fork of RiderClaudeTabs by Ragnaraven, rebuilt for IntelliJ 2026.1's reworked terminal and extended with conversation-derived tab names, shaped status icons and Remote Control. Licensed under MPL-2.0, as the original is.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.1

  • A session waiting on background agents was shown as finished. Stop fires when the response ends, not when the session's work does: a background fan-out and a subagent run both keep going past it, and Claude's own status field — which covers delegated work, not just the model turn — is the only signal that knows. Caught live on a session printing "waiting for 5 background agents to finish" under a ✓ tab: hook Stop at 15:58:03 over a session file that had read busy since 15:25:18 and still did at 16:00. That the correct reading was half an hour older is the point — Claude rewrites the file on state changes, so "old" says nothing about "stale", and this could not have been a freshness rule.
  • Most of Claude's notifications are not someone waiting on you. The filter knew about the 60-second idle nudge and treated the other eleven notification_type values as prompts — and because the status file holds one edge per session, each one overwrote the Stop or UserPromptSubmit underneath it. agent_completed was the worst of them: it fires when a background agent finishes, so a fan-out of five put five spurious ⚠ on the tab least likely to be looked at. elicitation_complete and elicitation_response marked the end of a wait as the start of one; auth_success ("Claude Code login successful") flipped a working tab. It is now an allowlist of the four that really do block — permission_prompt, worker_permission_prompt, elicitation_dialog, agent_needs_input — and an unrecognised type establishes nothing, because a missed block is still caught by Claude's own session file while a false one destroys what it was written over.
  • A /clear is not a death. SessionEnd now carries its reason, and clear / resume are read as what they are: in-place replacements where the process, the terminal and the tab all survive and only the session id rotates. They no longer paint ✗ while the pid-join hand-over catches up.
  • A turn that dies on an API error fires StopFailure, not Stop. Rate limit, overloaded, billing — none of them produced an edge, so the session kept its UserPromptSubmit and the session file's idle then won on age, leaving a turn that ran for minutes looking like one that never started. The event is now subscribed to.
  • SessionStart gained a fork source, which was falling through to "nothing has run yet". A forked conversation arrives with its history behind it, like resume.
  • shell is documented and handled for what it actually is. Claude only ever produces it when the status would otherwise be idle, so it means "at the prompt, with a detached background Bash still running" — a dev server, a watcher. A Bash tool call inside a turn reads as busy. It still shows as running, but a Stop is allowed to settle it, or an npm run dev left in the background would pin the tab for as long as the server is up.
  • The status hook script is rewritten. Its timestamp is now milliseconds on every platform: BSD date has no %N, so on macOS it had been falling back to whole seconds — which rounds a Stop backwards past the idle Claude wrote a fraction of a second earlier, the exact comparison the precedence rules turn on. Also: the Claude pid is resolved from the messaging socket or the process tree rather than assuming $PPID, the session id is validated before it becomes a filename, the payload is parsed first-match rather than last (a transcript excerpt can carry its own source), and the record is written to a temp file and renamed so the 400ms poll can never read a half-written one.
  • 494 unit tests.

1.0.36

  • "Is this tab still unnamed?" was answered in English only. The IDE's default terminal name is localised — 로컬 on a Korean IDE, ローカル on Japanese, 本地 on Chinese — and the check only knew Local / bash / pwsh. An untouched default tab therefore read as a name someone had deliberately chosen, everywhere that check is consulted: the spare-terminal sweep kept it, automatic naming refused to touch it, and restore treated it as meaningful.
  • The name is now read at runtime from the terminal plugin's own bundle key (local.terminal.default.name), so it is correct in whatever language the IDE is running — rather than a list that grows one language at a time. The three packs JetBrains ships are hard-coded as a fallback for when that lookup fails, read out of those plugins rather than guessed.
  • Numbered variants come along: 로컬 (2) counts, exactly as Local (2) always did.
  • Found by the diagnostic added in 1.0.32, which reported the tab with every other guard passing: '로컬'(pid=91000 generic=false claude=false children=0[] ours=false → keep).
  • 400 unit tests.

1.0.35

  • The six slash commands are gone — /tab, /tabs-status, /tabs-backup, /tabs-history, /tabs-restore, /tabs-clear. Every one had been overtaken: naming is automatic now, the IDE's own right-click → Rename Session covers the deliberate case (and the plugin never overwrites a title set there), and /tabs-history / /tabs-status duplicated Claude's /resume and claude agents with less information — they would happily offer to resume a session that was still running.
  • The three Node helpers and tab.sh that only existed to back them are gone too, and the five settings.json permissions they needed are withdrawn on upgrade rather than merely no longer added — otherwise an old install keeps allowing commands the plugin no longer ships.
  • Files left by earlier installs are removed on every start, not just on uninstall: a stale command that half-works is worse than none.
  • 394 unit tests (17 covering the removed scripts went with them).

1.0.34

  • Stops asking Claude to name the tab. The instruction the plugin injects into ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md told Claude to run rename-tab.sh at the start of every conversation, which spent a turn on something 1.0.33 now gets for free by reading the session name Claude already maintains. The instruction now says the opposite: don't name the tab unless the user asks.
  • What it still covers, because those cannot be read from anywhere: use the user's exact words when they do ask for a name, and never treat the status glyph as part of the name.
  • Any CLAUDE.md section an older version installed is removed on start, so this applies without any manual edit.

1.0.33

  • Tabs are named from Claude's own summary of the conversation. Claude Code keeps a name for each session in ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json and records where it came from: derived is built mechanically from the working directory (riderclaudetabs-29), while auto is Claude's own summary of what the conversation is about (설치 스크립트 초기 설정 프로세스 개선). Only auto and user are used; a directory-derived name tells the tab nothing it doesn't already know.
  • A name typed via /tab still outranks everything — that is an explicit choice. Below it, Claude's name now comes before the older fallbacks.
  • The label follows the conversation: it is re-applied when the tab is still generic, or when it is showing a name this plugin put there. A title someone typed into the tab strip is never overwritten.
  • This costs nothing at runtime and needs no cooperation from the conversation, unlike the instruction the plugin injects into ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md asking Claude to call rename-tab.sh at the start of every conversation — which spends a turn to do the same job.

1.0.32

  • The spare-terminal sweep now says why it did nothing. Twice in a row it silently skipped every tab and the log gave no way to tell which guard rejected them. Each candidate is now reported with the value of every input: '로컬'(pid=67036 generic=true claude=false children=0[] ours=false → CLOSE).
  • It retries for 20 seconds after a restore instead of running once. At the instant restore finishes the IDE's default shell can transiently own a child process — this machine's .zshrc ends in exec zsh — and a single shot reads that as "in use" and never looks again. Past the window it stops: by then a spare terminal is one someone has been looking at, and closing it would be a surprise rather than tidying.

1.0.31

  • The spare terminal is actually closed now. 1.0.29 added the cleanup and it never once fired: it asked the widget for a process id, but the IDE's own default tab reports its id through the backend session instead — STEP 3b: [로컬→PID67036(sess)] alongside skipNoPid=2 in the same poll. The pid came back null every time and every tab was skipped. It now goes through the same tab enumeration the rest of the plugin uses, which tries both routes. All the safety guards are unchanged.
  • Background Remote Control no longer leaves orphans behind. Running through $SHELL -l -i -c makes the server a child of the process we hold, so stopping only that parent left the real server reparented to launchd — seen as ppid=1 remote-control shells surviving IDE restarts, which the duplicate check would then read as a server already serving. The whole process tree is terminated on project close.

1.0.30

  • Background Remote Control actually starts now. 1.0.29's attempt failed with Cannot run program "claude" … error=2 (No such file or directory): an IDE launched from the Dock inherits a minimal PATH that has no ~/.local/bin, where the CLI installs itself. The pty attempt failed for the same reason and reported it as a bare InvocationTargetException: null.
  • It now runs through $SHELL -l -i -c, the same login and interactive flags the IDE's own terminal tab uses. Both flags are load-bearing: measured against a stripped environment, zsh -l -c 'command -v claude' still fails, because a login shell reads .zprofile while the PATH entry lives in .zshrc — which only an interactive shell sources.
  • Reflective failures are unwrapped before logging, so the next one names the actual cause instead of the wrapper.
  • 401 unit tests.

1.0.29

  • Coloured tab icons. Each tab gets a dot in the colour of its state — blue working, amber waiting, green finished, hollow grey idle, hollow red exited. The glyph stays: tabs this plugin spawned are reached through their widget and can't always be resolved to a Content to hang an icon on, and a tab without an icon still has to show its state. Tab label colour is not used — that lives in the tool window's internal JBTabs, the same layer that has broken repeatedly here; Content.setIcon is a plain, stable API.
  • Reopening leaves the same number of terminals it closed with. When the terminal tool window is active at startup the IDE creates a default tab of its own — measured at 68ms after the plugin starts, three seconds before restore fires — and restore then added the saved sessions on top. That spare tab is now closed, but only when a restore actually happened, only while it still has its default name, only with no Claude in it, and only when its shell has no child processes at all. Anything running in it, or a name someone chose, keeps it.
  • remoteControl.mode = "background" now works. Remote Control is interactive and exits at once without a terminal on the other end, which is why the first attempt at this mode looked simply broken. It now runs on a real pty (pty4j, which ships with the platform and is what the IDE's own terminal uses), with its output drained to remote-control-<project>.log. A plain pipe remains the fallback, and an immediate exit is reported rather than left looking like success.
  • Duplicate Remote Control servers are actually prevented now. The argv-plus-lsof scan was the only check and the log shows it never once fired — seven starts across restarts, twice inside a single IDE run. The server's pid is now recorded in rc-<project>.lock and checked directly, which doesn't depend on argv being readable or on lsof output shape. The scan stays, for servers started by hand.
  • 400 unit tests.

1.0.28

  • A finished chat stays ✓ across an IDE restart instead of reverting to ○. Restarting resumes every saved conversation, which fires SessionStart again, and that was mapped to Idle wholesale — so a chat you left finished came back marked as if it had never run a turn. The restart is the IDE's business, not the conversation's.
  • The hook now records SessionStart's source: startup and clear mean nothing has run yet (Idle), resume means an existing conversation picked back up at the prompt with its last turn behind it (Finished). compact fires mid-conversation, often mid-turn, so it says nothing about whether Claude is working and now leaves the current state alone rather than resetting it.
  • A hook file with no recorded source keeps the old meaning, so nothing changes until the updated script has run once.
  • 393 unit tests.

1.0.27

  • Restored tabs appear in about a second instead of nine. The spawns themselves were already parallel — three tabs in 6ms, their shells starting concurrently — so the wall-clock was almost entirely fixed waiting before the first spawn: a 3s head start plus a flat 5s "settle" sleep.
  • The settle now waits for the terminal tool window to stop changing rather than for the clock: it fires once the content count has held steady for 800ms, with the old 5s constant kept as a ceiling so a tool window that never settles can't block restore. The wait exists so leftover empty tabs the IDE remembered from workspace.xml can be closed before fresh ones are spawned — that still happens, it just stops costing five seconds when the tabs were in place after one.
  • The poll loop's head start drops from 3s to 1s, since readiness is now detected rather than assumed.

1.0.26

  • The indicator appears within a couple of seconds of a tab, instead of up to a minute later. Attaching used to happen only inside the save poll, which returns early during its startup grace — up to 60 seconds while restored tabs are still coming up. Measured on a real start: plugin up at 20:01:54, first attach at 20:02:21. Twenty-seven seconds of blank tabs, which is the first thing anyone notices.
  • The status loop now runs its own attach pass on a 1.5s throttle and starts 1.5s after the project opens rather than 4s. The poll still attaches too, which is what keeps handles fresh as tabs are moved between split panes.

1.0.25

  • The status indicator attaches to tabs this plugin spawned, using the widget it already holds. Measured on 2026.1: the tab managers reported one tab (an empty shell) while ContentManager held four, and the three they didn't know about were exactly the three the plugin had spawned — restored sessions and the Remote Control tab. Those are the tabs that most need the indicator, and every identity route missed them: no shell PID, getSession() throws, and their widgets are TerminalWidgetBridge over com.jetbrains.rdserver.terminal.BackendTtyConnector.
  • But the plugin created those tabs, so it has held the widget keyed by session id since spawn time (spawnedWidgets). Painting a title needs nothing more than that. No reflection, no PID, no TERM_SESSION_ID — the earlier routes stay as fallbacks for tabs opened by hand.
  • 382 unit tests.

1.0.24

  • Second route for attaching the status indicator, via ContentManager. The backend and frontend tab managers intermittently report zero tabs while ContentManager still holds every one of them (observed: Backend has 0 tabs alongside contents=3), which left the TERM_SESSION_ID bridge with nothing to read an id from. The identity probe showed the widgets are TerminalWidgetBridge and do expose getSession(), so the id is reachable from there.
  • The search matches on value, not on accessor name: it walks a couple of levels of zero-argument accessors and takes the first object whose string form contains a TERM_SESSION_ID the hook has already recorded. The shape inside these objects has moved twice across releases, so hard-coding the next accessor name would buy exactly one version; the id being a UUID is the part that stays true. Bounded by an accessor allowlist, a depth limit, identity tracking and a node budget — a widget transitively reaches the whole editor.
  • The identity probe now prints the reachable values and the UUIDs being looked for, so a failure says which of the two is missing rather than just that nothing matched.
  • 382 unit tests.

1.0.23

  • Fixes a live background agent being read as dead. The installed CLI is a versioned binary whose filename is the version — ~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.226 — and sessions the daemon launches run it directly instead of through the ~/.local/bin/claude shim. Every name-based check missed them, so a running background agent looked dead, its session looked restorable, and restore ran claude --resume against it — which Claude refuses outright with "currently running as a background agent". Recognition now also matches the install path.
  • The liveness check the restore path uses deliberately counts non-interactive sessions too: a running background agent is a reason not to restore its session, even though it could never have been a tab.
  • Identity probe for the remaining status gap. When nothing can be attached, the log now dumps what is actually reachable from each terminal Content — widget class plus any member that could carry a session id or the process environment. Both existing routes have been seen failing on this platform (shell PIDs absent or belonging to a different tab; backend/frontend tab managers intermittently reporting zero tabs while ContentManager holds several), and this replaces guessing at another API with one log excerpt.
  • 374 unit tests.

1.0.22

  • The status indicator now attaches by TERM_SESSION_ID, not by process id. This is what makes it actually appear on IntelliJ 2026.1's reworked terminal. The PID route collapses there: the platform hands out shell PIDs belonging to empty tabs while the tabs actually hosting Claude report no PID at all — observed on a real install as three enumerated tabs whose shells were childless zsh, alongside six live Claude sessions on shells the enumeration never mentioned. Walking shell pid → child claude cannot work when the shell pid belongs to a different tab.
  • The bridge has no PID in it anywhere: the backend tab exposes its TERM_SESSION_ID, every process the tab spawns inherits it, and the status hook records TERM_SESSION_ID → sessionId from inside the session. A terminal reused for a second session resolves to the session in it now, decided by timestamp rather than by directory order.
  • Additive: tabs the PID walk does resolve keep using it, and this only fills the gaps.
  • The status heartbeat now reports termMap=N, which separates "no session has fired a hook yet" (hooks missing, or every session predates their install and needs restarting) from "mappings exist but no tab matched one".
  • 370 unit tests.

1.0.21

  • Fixes duplicate tabs on install / project reload. Restore spawned a tab for every session in the restore file without checking whether that session was still running. Installing the plugin reloads the project without killing anything, so every session was still alive in the tab it had always been in — and each got a second tab beside it running claude --resume against the same conversation. A session that is already running is now never restored. Matching covers both the reported and the canonical id, since a resumed process reports a rotated one and the restore file stores the canonical.
  • Remote Control can run without a tab. Set "mode": "background" under remoteControl in ~/.claude/intellij-claude-terminal/config.json: the server runs detached with its output going to ~/.claude/intellij-claude-terminal/remote-control-<project>.log, and is stopped when the project closes. Note this trades away what the tab is for — the connection state and the runtime w (worktree) toggle. If the server needs a TTY it will exit immediately, and the log line says so.
  • 363 unit tests.

1.0.20

  • Remote Control starts automatically, once per project. On IDE start the plugin opens a terminal tab running claude remote-control for the project directory, so this machine's sessions can be driven from claude.ai/code and the Claude mobile app without setting anything up. This exposes control of local Claude sessions to your Claude account for as long as the IDE is open. Turn it off with "remoteControl": {"enabled": false} in ~/.claude/intellij-claude-terminal/config.json.
  • Never a second server for the same directory. Before starting, the plugin looks for a remote-control process already serving that path — including one you started by hand in another terminal — by matching argv and then reading the process's working directory. The rc alias is matched as a whole token, so a path containing src/ can't be mistaken for it.
  • The Remote Control tab is not tracked as a chat. It hosts a server, and the session that server pre-creates belongs to the server — tracking it would put it in the restore file and bring it back after a restart as a plain tab running claude --resume against it.
  • The project name is passed as --name so several machines and projects stay distinguishable on the phone. It is shell-quoted: it is a directory name reaching a real shell.
  • spawnMode (same-dir / worktree / session) and extraArgs are configurable; an unrecognised spawn mode is dropped rather than passed through to fail inside the tab.
  • Diagnosability: a status heartbeat now logs every ~minute with the three inputs that decide whether a glyph appears (tab count, tracked sessions, signal readings). The most likely failure — no glyphs at all — used to produce no log output whatsoever.
  • 353 unit tests.

1.0.19

  • Claude Code status on the terminal tab. Each tab is prefixed with a glyph for the state of the Claude session running in it: ● Working, ⚠ Waiting for input, ✓ Finished, ○ Idle, ✕ Exited. The tab tooltip spells the state out. Nothing else about the terminal changes — no new tool window, no new panel, no change to how you launch claude.
  • Hook-driven, with a reconciliation pass. Hooks on SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Notification, Stop and SessionEnd record each transition the moment it happens. Claude Code's own per-session status field (~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json: busy/shell/idle/waiting) is read alongside it, which covers sessions that started before the hooks were installed, permission prompts that emit no Notification, and a Claude that was killed rather than exiting. Newer signal wins, except that a stale idle can't downgrade a hook-established Finished. SubagentStop is deliberately not subscribed — a subagent finishing is not the turn finishing.
  • The glyph never reaches disk. Decoration is applied to the live tab title only and stripped at every point a title is read back, so names.json, the restore files and history keep bare names. Without this, a restored tab would come back literally called ● backend.
  • settings.json is now edited as JSON, not as text. Hook and permission installation parses the file, edits the tree and re-serialises. The previous regex string-surgery assumed one particular file shape and produced invalid JSON on any other — which takes Claude Code down with it. Unrelated settings, the user's own hooks, and their matchers are preserved verbatim; a file that can't be parsed is left strictly alone and the failure is logged. The pre-edit file is copied once to ~/.claude/intellij-claude-terminal/settings.json.bak. Uninstall removes our entries the same way instead of leaving dangling commas behind.
  • Status runs on its own loop, separate from the 5s save poll, at a 400ms cadence over a handful of small files, touching only the tabs whose state actually changed. It does not use a WatchService: the JDK has no native file watcher on macOS and falls back to a polling implementation with a 10s sensitivity, which would be slower than this.
  • Built and verified against IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1.3 (IU-261.25134.95) on Gradle 9.7 / JDK 21.
  • 323 unit tests — new coverage for the decorate/strip round-trip invariant across every state, the hook-vs-session-file precedence table, status reading against real Claude Code file shapes, and the settings.json patcher (idempotency, preservation of foreign hooks, refusal to touch malformed JSON).

1.0.18

  • Window-state serialization: tabs are tracked by which Rider window they live in, not by their working directory. A Claude session opened from a sibling folder (e.g. a git worktree at D:\Dev\MyApp-feature-branch) whose terminal tab is hosted in the main project's Rider window is now correctly tracked in that project's restore file. Pre-1.0.18 the cwd-prefix filter dropped these sessions as "cross-project leaks" and they never auto-restored.
  • Worktree-resume transcript lookup: when a session originally started in one folder is later resumed by sid from a different folder (typical worktree workflow: cd ../MyApp-feature && claude --resume <sid>), Claude keeps appending to the original transcript path. The transcript-existence check now falls back to scanning all project dirs after the cwd-derived path misses, so the session is no longer rejected with skipNoTranscript and lands in the restore file like any other.
  • Tab discovery is now authoritative. The poll() tab-walk re-contributes to the saved session list (it was disabled in the early 1.0.17 work after a canonical-id collision caused stale sids to shadow real ones; the underlying collision is now fixed, so tab-walk is trustworthy again). SessionsDirScanner stays as a fallback for tabs the platform APIs lose.
  • DockManager-based 5th tab source: popped-out terminal tabs in floating windows are now enumerated via com.intellij.openapi.fileEditor.impl.DockManager.containers. Reflective access with try/catch fallback — missing API on older IDEs degrades to "no popout coverage" rather than a crash. Combined with the existing 4 enumeration sources, this catches tabs across split panes, island groups, hidden-under-overflow, minimized tool windows, and popped-out floating windows.
  • Cross-project arbitration: when two open project windows would both claim the same session, the project whose tab-walk found it wins. The other project's scanner defers. Prevents the same sid from being saved into two restore files.
  • Canonical-id cache correction: canonicalSessionIdFor now always re-checks Strategy 1 (transcript-on-disk) before honoring cached results. A stale Strategy 3 mtime-fallback guess gets corrected the instant the real transcript appears. Fixes two distinct alive sids collapsing into one canonical (which previously caused the scanner to skip the second as skipAlreadyHave and the save loop to drop it from the restore file).
  • names.json auto-applied to live tabs. The poll loop now re-applies a stored name when the live tab title is generic ("Local"/"Claude") or an AI overlay glyph. Manual user-typed titles are still respected. Effect: setting a name via /tab, migration backfill, or direct names.json edit shows up on the tab strip within ~5 seconds.
  • Two-poll-grace eviction. A sid missing from one poll's scanner output is no longer instantly evicted from the restore file — it's preserved one cycle (the grace), then evicted if still missing on the second poll. Forgives single-poll races (Claude restart, brief PID gap, scanner momentary skip) without keeping zombies forever. Worst-case eviction lag: ~10s at the 5s poll cadence.
  • Authoritative saveState with name preservation. When the scanner returns a non-empty list, existing restore entries whose sid isn't in the new list are dropped (the eviction path for dead zombies and cross-project leaks). Descriptive names from the prior file are preserved when the scanner returns a generic name for the same sid — restore-file-only names from sessions that pre-date names.json survive.
  • /tabs-backup rewritten. Source switched from "whatever's in the restore file" to ~/.claude/sessions/*.json (Claude's own alive list). Now actually backs up every currently-alive session, catching anything the poll lagged on or dropped. Updates both the restore file AND history.json in one go.
  • 248+ unit tests — new scenarios cover canonical-id cache correction, two-poll-grace eviction + recovery, authoritative replace with descriptive-name preservation, the tab-walk-pollution regression shape, JSON cwd extraction with Windows-style double-backslash escapes, and the rewritten /tabs-backup behavior.

1.0.17

  • Saves no longer trust the live widget title for tab names. A new names.json store keyed by sessionId is the durable source of truth. The save loop reads from there ahead of the legacy fallback chain, so the JetBrains AI Assistant overlay corrupting the live title with a status glyph (e.g. ✳ Claude Code) can no longer reach the saved name. Fixes restored tabs coming back as ✳ Claude Code instead of their real names.
  • 3-tier rolling backup of the restore file. New backups/active-sessions-<projectHash>-{1,2,3}.json, rotated on every non-empty save. Load fallback now: live → backup-1 → backup-2 → backup-3 → existing snapshots/. Recovery from a corrupted live file is automatic, with an idea.log line confirming which tier was used.
  • User-closed sessions persist to disk. New user-closed-<projectHash>.json per project, hydrated on plugin startup and atomically appended at close-verify time. Pre-1.0.17 this was in-memory only — a hard kill / Task Manager / power loss between the X-click and the next save resurrected the just-closed tab on restart.
  • Empty-write bypass closed. removeFromRestoreImmediately used to write the restore file directly, skipping the empty-write guard. On false-positive close events during IDE-update tab thrash this wiped every session to []. Now routed through saveState, which preserves the file when subtraction would empty it.
  • Startup-grace gate on poll(). During the first 60s with restore-spawn still pending, the save loop is a no-op. Avoids empty-active overwrites while the spawned tabs are still warming up.
  • AI overlay regex extended for U+2731–U+273F (Dingbats heavy-asterisk family). The old range stopped at U+28FF and missed ✳ (U+2733) — the glyph Claude Code currently emits.
  • Names follow resumed sessions. When the poll loop sees a rotated→canonical sessionId after claude --resume, the canonical sid's name is mirrored onto the rotated sid in names.json, so future lookups under either id resolve.
  • /tabs-status is now ~10x faster. Plugin maintains project-index.json on every project open; the skill reads it (~5ms) instead of cold-starting Node (~500–800ms on Windows). Total drops from ~900ms to under 100ms. Node fallback retained for the no-ancestor-match edge case.
  • Startup self-test banner in idea.log surfaces the load-bearing API state (terminal tool window, frontend/backend tab managers, DockManager, names.json health) for diagnosability across future IDE drifts.
  • 223 unit tests — 23 new covering names.json upsert/cache/alias/prune, persistent userClosed round-trip + per-project isolation, backup rotation, load fallback through backup tiers, and dingbats regex coverage.

1.0.16

  • Fixes X-button closes being silently dropped right after restart — the 30-second startup grace introduced in 1.0.15 was too coarse: it correctly ignored Rider's tool-window re-layout events, but it also ate legitimate user closes that happened in the same window (the most natural moment to close an unwanted tab is right after seeing it auto-restore). The grace is gone; a contentRemoved is now disambiguated by capturing the underlying TerminalWidget and checking 1.5 seconds later whether it's still attached to any Content in the tool window. Shuffles re-bind the widget to a fresh Content within the same swing tick; real closes leave it orphaned. Works regardless of how recently the plugin attached.
  • Restore file rewritten synchronously on confirmed close — used to wait for the next 5-second poll, which meant a user who clicked X then immediately closed Rider could lose the close (the next poll never runs). Now the verify step writes the restore file atomically the moment the close is confirmed.
  • Verify delay shortened 3s → 1.5s. Widget-attachment is decidable as soon as Rider completes the swing tick that holds the shuffle.

1.0.15

  • Fixes "tabs go missing after restart" — the ContentManagerListener was treating Rider's tool-window re-layout events (fired while restoring tabs, splits, popouts at startup) as user closes, then subtracting those sessions from the restore file forever. A 30-second startup grace where every contentRemoved was ignored, plus a 3-second deferred process-alive check for events past the grace. (Superseded by the 1.0.16 widget-attachment check, which catches the same re-layout case without the false-negative on fast user closes.)
  • Fixes descriptive tab names being silently replaced with "Local" across restart. The save-loop union was unconditionally letting the live tab title overlay the saved name, so a freshly-spawned tab whose title still read "Local" (Claude hadn't repainted yet after --resume) would clobber the descriptive name on disk within 5 seconds. Now a generic name can never beat a descriptive one — other fields (cwd, bypass) still propagate.
  • Clears Marketplace verifier warning on the spawn-new-tab call. TerminalToolWindowManager.createNewSession is annotated @ApiStatus.Internal in 2025.x+ and the verifier rejected the direct invocation. The call is now reflective, so there's no compile-time binary reference for the verifier to flag; runtime behaviour is unchanged.
  • Extensive logging on every close-detection branch — search idea.log for [ClaudeTabs][close] and [ClaudeTabs][verify] to see exactly why each event was kept or ignored.

1.0.14

  • Bundled shell scripts (rename-tab.sh, session-start-hook.sh) now ship with LF line endings, fixing the $'\r': command not found error on macOS / Linux (issue #1). Three layers of defense: .gitattributes pin, normalised source files, and runtime CR stripping at deploy time.
  • Minimum platform bumped to IntelliJ 2026.1 (build 261). Migrated off the deprecated createShellWidget to createNewSession; built against IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.x with Kotlin 2.3.
  • Restore file is now a high-water-mark union of existing + new sessions, minus sessions the user explicitly closed. A missed poll can no longer evict a session that's actually still there.
  • Tab-X / right-click → Close Tab / Close Others / Close All are recognised as user-initiated closes; the session is dropped from auto-restore. Window-X / project shutdown is NOT a close — sessions survive across IDE restarts as intended.
  • /tab (and right-click → Rename Session) now persists the new name to the restore file and a fresh snapshot immediately, instead of waiting for the next 5-second poll. Crash-safe across the gap.
  • Restore file writes are atomic (tmp + rename). Snapshot filenames use a double-underscore delimiter so sibling projects with overlapping path prefixes (e.g. foo vs foo-mobile) can no longer cross-prune each other.
  • Auto-restored tabs (and Rider's workspace.xml-restored shells) no longer disappear from save tracking. Fixes "only 2 of 5 tabs come back" on Rider 2026.1.
  • Restored terminal tabs actually run claude --resume on spawn — previously shells started cold and only the focused tab ever executed the resume.
  • Restore file is never deleted on an empty poll. A single transient "0 active sessions" cycle can no longer wipe your saved multi-session state.
  • Generic saved names ("Local", "Local (2)") no longer pin userDefinedTitle, so the resumed Claude chat title surfaces naturally.
  • Tab enumeration now sweeps ContentManager as a fallback — fixes /tab reporting "no tab found" for restored sessions whose tab the reworked managers don't list.
  • Direct widget tracking for tabs the plugin spawns — /tab renames go straight to the cached widget reference without re-enumerating, so restored sessions can always be renamed even when the reworked managers don't list them.
  • Save loop now scans ~/.claude/sessions/ directly (filtered by project cwd) instead of relying solely on the platform's tab APIs to enumerate which Claude processes are alive. Fixes "10 tabs spawned, only 1 saved" on Rider 2026.1 where freshly-spawned widgets don't expose their ttyConnector via reflection.

1.0.13

  • Auto-restore opens saved sessions in fresh tabs — fixes wrong-chat-in-wrong-tab when multiple projects are open.

1.0.12

  • Auto-restore now covers sessions in unnamed tabs too.
  • /tabs-history survives crashes (sessions recorded within a minute of starting).

1.0.11

  • Fixes restore and history when multiple projects are open at once.

1.0.10

  • Fixes "no tabs auto-restored on load" caused by sessions leaking between sibling projects.

1.0.9

  • /tab is roughly 2× faster on first use.

1.0.8

  • Stops silently wiping history.json on transient read failures (AV, OneDrive, indexer locks).
  • Atomic writes for history.json.

1.0.7

  • All /tabs-* commands now scope to the current project by default. Pass --all for the global view.
  • /tabs-clear preserves history.json.

1.0.6

  • Restore works again after a PC restart that preserves tab titles.
  • /tabs-history defaults to the current project.
  • Fixes snapshot mixups between projects with similar paths (e.g. MyApp vs MyApp-mobile).

1.0.5

  • Compatibility with Rider 2026.1 — coexists with the JetBrains AI Assistant / Claude Agent panel.
  • Tab names hold against the AI Assistant title overlay.
  • Resuming a session no longer fails with "No conversation found" after Claude rotates the session id.

1.0.3

  • /tabs-history, /tabs-restore, /tabs-status render as markdown tables.
  • History age column shows seconds for recent entries.

1.0.2

  • Cleaner slash-command output — no more Node script dumps in the terminal.
  • /tabs-history and /tabs-restore show a built-in choice menu.

1.0.1

  • /tabs-restore and /tabs-history print the claude --resume command instead of trying to run it (nested resume always failed).

1.0.0 — Initial release

  • Auto-rename terminal tabs to match the active Claude conversation.
  • Session save/restore across IDE restarts.
  • Slash commands: /tab, /tabs-status, /tabs-backup, /tabs-history, /tabs-restore, /tabs-clear.
  • Auto-install of scripts, commands, and permissions on startup; clean uninstall on removal.

registryKey.description: Defer to JetBrains AI Assistant / Anthropic Claude Code plugin when present (informational log only as of 1.0.5). Set to false for legacy 1.0.3 behavior.

Bypass rate-limiting on high-frequency log lines (AI overlay re-apply, restore-pending). When true, every event logs. When false, rate-limited to once per minute per key. Equivalent to enabling DEBUG logging for #com.claudetabs.
